title: Investigation of Kaposi’s Sarcoma-Associated Herpesvirus Replication Kinetics
author: Singh, Bose, et al.
materials: where sides of long coverslip (22 x

steps.title: Prepare silanized slides
steps.instruction: Soak slides in 1 % SDS for ≥30 min, wash with warm water (45‑50 °C) then distilled water, soak in 2:1 HNO₃:HCl for 12 h in sealed tray (fume hood), rinse 3‑4 times with distilled water (3‑4 min each), rinse with methanol in a Coplin jar, soak in 4 % Amino‑Silane in methanol for 1 h at 20‑25 °C with gentle shaking, rinse with methanol then three washes with distilled water (3 min each), rinse with 95 % ethanol, air‑dry, place in a desiccator airtight for 12‑24 h (use within 96 h).

substeps.instruction: a. Soak slides in 1 % SDS solution for ≥30 min.
b. Remove with forceps, wash with warm water (45‑50 °C) then distilled water.
c. Soak in HNO₃:HCl (2:1) for 12 h in sealed tray (fume hood).
d. Rinse thoroughly with distilled water 3‑4 times (3‑4 min each).
e. Rinse with methanol in Coplin jar (up‑and‑down motion).
f. Soak in 4 % Amino‑Silane in methanol for 1 h at 20‑25 °C, mild shaking.
g. Rinse with methanol, then three washes with distilled water (3 min each).
h. Rinse with 95 % ethanol, air‑dry, store in desiccator for 12‑24 h; avoid storage >96 h.

steps.title: Make nucleotide analog stocks
steps.instruction: Prepare 10 mM CldU by dissolving 128.4 mg CldU in 48.9 mL H₂O; freeze at –20 °C. Prepare 10 mM IdU by dissolving 205.5 mg IdU in 58.05 mL H₂O, add 200 µL 10 N NaOH, freeze at –20 °C.

steps.title: Prepare 10 % sarcosine solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 100 g L‑Sarcosine in 850 mL H₂O, then bring volume to 1 L with H₂O.

steps.title: Prepare 0.5 M EDTA pH 8.0
steps.instruction: Dissolve 186.5 g EDTA in 800 mL H₂O, adjust pH to 8.0 with 10 N NaOH, then bring volume to 1 L.

steps.title: Prepare 1.4 % InCert agarose plugs
steps.instruction: Make 1.4 % InCert agarose in PBS, aliquot 1 mL into 1.5 mL micro‑centrifuge tubes, store at 4 °C.

steps.title: Prepare 0.7 % low‑melting agarose
steps.instruction: Prepare 0.7 % low‑melting agarose in Tris‑acetate EDTA or Tris‑borate EDTA buffer, pH 8.0.

steps.title: Make storage buffer for plugs
steps.instruction: For 1 L, add 100 mL 0.5 M EDTA and 10 mL 1 M Tris‑HCl pH 8.0 to 890 mL autoclaved distilled water (final 50 mM EDTA, 10 mM Tris‑HCl, pH 8).

steps.title: Make pre‑digestion buffer for plugs
steps.instruction: For 1 L, add 10 mL 1 M MgCl₂ and 10 mL 1 M Tris‑HCl pH 8.0 to 980 mL autoclaved distilled water (final 10 mM MgCl₂, 10 mM Tris‑HCl, pH 8).

steps.title: Pulse cells and embed in agarose plugs
steps.instruction: Harvest BC3 cells (500 × g, 5 min), resuspend 10 mL medium, add 125 µL 10 mM CldU, top to 50 mL, incubate 4 h at 5 % CO₂. Pellet, repeat with 125 µL 10 mM IdU for a second 4 h pulse. Wash cells in ice‑cold PBS, resuspend at 3 × 10⁷ cells/mL in ice‑cold PBS. Melt 1 mL 0.7 % InCert agarose (PBS) 4‑5 min, equilibrate agarose and cell suspension at 42 °C 5 min, mix equal volumes (final density 1.5 × 10⁷ cells/mL). Dispense ~100 µL into plug caster wells (≈1 plug per 100 µL), solidify 30‑60 min at 4 °C, store plugs in storage buffer at 4 °C.

substeps.instruction: CldU pulse: harvest, resuspend, add CldU, top up, incubate 4 h.
IdU pulse: repeat harvesting, resuspend, add IdU, top up, incubate 4 h.
Embed cells: wash, resuspend 3 × 10⁷ cells/mL, melt agarose, equilibrate both at 42 °C, mix 1:1, dispense 100 µL per plug, solidify 30‑60 min at 4 °C, store.

steps.title: Proteinase K digestion of plugs
steps.instruction: In a 50 mL tube add 25 mL 1 % sarcosine in 0.5 M EDTA (plug digestion buffer). Push plugs into buffer, add 0.25 mL Proteinase K (20 mg/mL) per 25 mL buffer, incubate at 50 °C water bath. After 24 h replace buffer with fresh 1 % sarcosine/0.5 M EDTA, add fresh Proteinase K, incubate another 24 h at 50 °C. Repeat buffer change and incubation for a third 24‑h period.

steps.title: Prepare radiolabeled hybridization probes
steps.instruction: Dilute 25 ng template DNA (NotI fragment of pBS‑PuroA) to 33 µL, boil 5 min, ice 5 min, brief centrifuge at 4 °C. Add 5 µL Octa‑deoxynucleotide in 10× labeling buffer, 6 µL dNTP mix (2 µL each dATP, dGTP, dTTP), 5 µL α‑P32‑dCTP (3000 Ci/mmol, 50 µCi). Mix, incubate 37 °C 1 h. Terminate with 5 µL 200 mM EDTA pH 8.0. Clean up with PCR cleanup kit, elute probe in 50 µL H₂O. Handle all radioactivity in designated area with proper shielding and waste disposal.

steps.title: Gelase/Agarase digestion and YOYO‑1 staining
steps.instruction: Cut 3‑4 agarose slices (2‑3 mm thick) from the Southern‑blot band region, wash with TE8 buffer. From each slice cut a ~2 mm‑wide piece. Equilibrate pieces in TE8 + 100 mM NaCl + 0.1 % β‑mercaptoethanol 1 h at 4 °C. Transfer each piece to a microcentrifuge tube, add 100‑150 µL digestion buffer, equilibrate 45 °C 5 min. Melt at 68‑72 °C 15‑20 min, cool to 45 °C 2‑3 min, add 2‑3 µL Gelase (or agarase, 42 °C) and digest ≥3‑4 h (Gelase at 45 °C, agarase at 42 °C). Add 0.1 µL YOYO‑1 dye and β‑mercaptoethanol to 5 % final; stain 12‑16 h (DNA visible after 1‑2 h).

steps.title: Stretch DNA on silanized slides and fix
steps.instruction: In a Coplin jar, use a cut yellow tip (20‑200 µL) to spread 7 µL YOYO‑1‑stained DNA from one edge of a 22 × 40 mm coverslip onto a silanized slide (use 4 µL for 22 × 22 mm coverslip). Denature by immersing slides in denaturation buffer 15 min (≤20 min total). Prepare fixation solution by adding glutaraldehyde to denaturation solution, fix slides 5 min. Wash sequentially with 70 % ethanol (3 washes, 2‑3 min each), then 95 % ethanol (2‑3 min), then 100 % ethanol (2‑3 min). Replace slides in methanol + 0.1 % β‑mercaptoethanol for 10 min, air‑dry at 20‑25 °C. Assemble a hybridization chamber by placing small coverslips (22 × 22 mm) on the slide and adding 2‑3 µL hybridization buffer under and over the coverslip edges to adhere them.

steps.title: Prepare FISH and immunostaining buffers
steps.instruction: Make 20× SSC stock, dilute as needed. Prepare solutions: (1) 4× SSC + 40 % formamide (2 jars); (2) 2× SSC + 1 % SDS (2 jars); (3) 2× SSC + 0.1 % NP‑40 (1 jar); (4) 4× SSC + 0.1 % NP‑40 (4 jars); (5) 1× PBS + 0.03 % NP‑40 (3 jars); (6) blocking buffer: 3 % BSA in 1× PBS. Prepare detection mixes (20 µL per slide): Mix 1/3 – Neutr‑Avidin Alexa 350 1:20 in blocking buffer; Mix 2 – Biotinylated anti‑Avidin 1:20; Mix 4 – Biotinylated anti‑Avidin 1:20, mouse anti‑IdU 1:10, rat anti‑CldU 1:10; Mix 5 – Neutr‑Avidin Alexa 350 1:20, Alexa 594‑anti‑mouse 1:10, Alexa 488‑anti‑rat 1:10.

steps.title: Hybridize biotinylated KSHV probes
steps.instruction: For each slide, add 94 µL hybridization buffer and 2 µL of each biotinylated KSHV probe (make a separate tube per slide). Denature probe mix at 95 °C 5 min, centrifuge, pipette into the open side of the hybridization chamber. Incubate slides 12‑16 h at 37 °C in a humid box.

steps.title: Sequential FISH detection and immunostaining
steps.instruction: Remove coverslip with razor blade. Rinse slides in 2× SSC + 1 % SDS (Coplin jar). Wash fresh 2× SSC + 1 % SDS 5 min. Wash 4× SSC + 40 % formamide (pre‑equilibrated 45 °C) 5 min, moving slides up‑and‑down 2‑3 times. Rinse 2× SSC + 0.1 % NP‑40 at 20‑25 °C. Wash 4× SSC + 0.1 % NP‑40 four times, 5 min each, at 20‑25 °C (different jars). Rinse 1× PBS + 0.03 % NP‑40 at 20‑25 °C. Apply 20 µL blocking buffer onto DNA region, cover with coverslip, incubate 20‑30 min at 20‑25 °C in humid chamber. Remove coverslip, add 20 µL detection mix 1, cover, incubate 20 min at 20‑25 °C. Rinse PBS + 0.03 % NP‑40, apply detection mix 2, incubate 20 min (same conditions). Rinse, apply detection mix 3, incubate 20 min. Rinse, apply detection mix 4, incubate 1 h at 20‑25 °C. Rinse, apply detection mix 5, incubate 1 h at 20‑25 °C. Final rinse in fresh 1× PBS + 0.03 % NP‑40, wipe excess, add 15 µL antifade reagent, place coverslip, seal with colorless nail polish, store at 4 °C ≥1 h before imaging.

steps.title: Mount slides and acquire images
steps.instruction: Capture fluorescence images at 60× magnification on a suitable microscope (e.g., Olympus IX70), acquire each color channel separately, then merge using ImageJ or equivalent software.

description: Single molecule analysis of the replicated DNA (SMARD) is a technique that precisely identifies regions undergoing replication on individual DNA molecules. This method can be applied to study the replication dynamics of cellular genomes, or of pathogens including bacteria and viruses (For example, Kaposi’s sarcoma associated herpesvirus, KSHV).1,3,4,5 In this protocol, we provide a step-by-step description of an adaptation of the original SMARD technique that enables detection of replication initiation sites on individual KSHV genomes using fluorescence microscopy. This version is optimized for episomal KSHV genomes maintained in latently infected cells; analysis of integrated viral genomes (e.g., HPV) would require additional considerations such as mapping of integration junctions, restriction-site availability, and potential sequence deletions. The approach can be further modified for use with other integrated viruses or pathogens. SMARD has been used to define where replication initiates, the direction and progression of replication forks, and the influence of regulatory or environmental factors on replication dynamics.6,7,8 To analyze a specific genomic region, locus-specific probes are used for orientation and detection by immunofluorescence. Here, we examined replication origin activity and fork progression on the KSHV genome using the KSHV-positive BC3 cell line, which maintains 80–100 latent viral genome copies as chromatinized episomes.2,9,10 Sequential labeling with halogenated nucleotides 5′-iodo-2′-deoxyuridine (IdU) and 5′-chloro-2′-deoxyuridine (CldU) enables visualization of replication fork direction and abundance at single-molecule resolution. KSHV DNA molecules are distinguished from host DNA by hybridization with biotinylated, KSHV-specific probes detected by fluorescence in situ hybridization. The labeled KSHV double-stranded DNA molecules incorporate nucleotide analogs throughout their length, allowing visualization over background fluorescence.
